retained_input_notes.source_note: Regime rule: general secretary. Najibullah took the party post 4 May 1986 and the presidency 30 Nov 1987; since is the party date. worldstatesmen.org/Afghanistan.html returned 404 twice this run.
Regime rule: first secretary (since 13 Apr 1985); head of state since 22 Nov 1982. worldstatesmen.org/Albania.html returned 404 twice this run.

worldstatesmen lists 20 Sep 1979, Wikipedia says he took office 21 Sep 1979; the inauguration date is used. No prime minister (post abolished 1978-1991).

The constitution as in force in 1990 set a single six-year term with no immediate re-election (Wikipedia); must_leave_by is 8 Jul 1995. The 1994 reform that later let him run again is after the start date.
Parliamentary system: the chancellor directs the executive; the federal president is recorded in also.
Premier from 16 Jan 1967; the office was retitled Prime Minister 10 May 1969, which is the since used.

Ruler (Hakim) from 2 Nov 1961, styled Emir from 16 Aug 1971; the Party pillar is the Al Khalifa family council. The PM headed the State Council from 10 Jan 1970 (Wikipedia) and took the PM title 16 Aug 1971 (worldstatesmen); the title date is used.
Ershad took the presidency 11 Dec 1983; the Jatiya Party was founded 1 Jan 1986 and is the tie the polity table carries.
worldstatesmen gives 7 Nov 1989, Wikipedia 7 Sep 1989; the election was 4 Sep 1989 so the September date is used.
No prime minister 1964-1998; the king governed directly through the Lhengye Zhungtshog, which is the Party pillar. No formally designated heir sourced for 1 Jan 1990.
Four-year term ending 6 Aug 1993 per both sources; the 1967 constitution's ban on consecutive re-election was not separately fetched, so must_leave_by rests on the term end alone.
Acting from 13 Jul 1980, elected by the National Assembly 18 Jul 1980.

Start-date rule: Sarney not Collor. Sarney was acting president from 15 Mar 1985 and president from 21 Apr 1985; since is the day he took the executive. Collor won the runoff of 17 Dec 1989 and is the also row as president-elect.
worldstatesmen lists 4 Oct 1967, Wikipedia 5 Oct 1967; Wikipedia's date used. Prime Minister himself since 1 Jan 1984. No crown prince proclamation sourced for 1990, so heir is null.

On 1 Jan 1990 the party was still the BCP (renamed BSP April 1990); bg_bsp is the polity table's id for it. Mladenov took the party 10 Nov 1989 and the State Council 17 Nov 1989. Atanasov's dates conflict between the two cited sources: Wikipedia gives 21 Mar 1986 - 3 Feb 1990, worldstatesmen 24 Mar 1986 - 8 Feb 1990; the row takes Wikipedia's, and both are a fact of 1 Jan 1990 either way.
Regime rule: general secretary, so Heng Samrin; Hun Sen, who ran the government, is the also row. Hun Sen was acting from 26 Dec 1984.
No prime minister (post abolished 25 Jan 1984 - 26 Apr 1991).
Parliamentary system: the prime minister directs the executive. Hnatyshyn took over as Governor General only on 29 Jan 1990.

Pereira held the party's general secretaryship on 1 Jan 1990 (he handed it to Pires only in July 1990). One-party state, so the party leader/president is the face, not the prime minister.

Brigadier general who took power as chairman of the Military Committee for National Recovery on 1 Sep 1981; by 1990 he ruled through the RDC, the sole legal party under the 1986 constitution, so the tie is the party rather than the Army pillar. He also held the prime ministership himself (no separate PM on 1 Jan 1990).
Took power 7 Jun 1982 (acting head of state), formally president from 29 Oct 1982; the earlier date is used as the start of his rule. Led UNIR from its founding on 24 Jun 1984.

REFUSED: tie. The sourced facts are George Vassiliou (President of the Republic since 28 Feb 1988, born 20 May 1931), whom the fetched Wikipedia page describes as an INDEPENDENT elected with AKEL's support; Cyprus's polity has no pillars. The cy_akel tie the data pass wrote was the backing party, not a membership, and its own note conceded that the Communist bloc it produced overstated a centrist technocrat. A backing is not a tie the schema knows, so the row is refused on 2026-09-05: name and tie nulled, office and dates kept, and Cyprus is described from its chamber until Ridge rules or the schema gains a sourced way to say 'independent'. Presidential system: the president is the executive. worldstatesmen's Cyprus page lists him but the extraction could not read the Republic's post-1977 lines, so Wikipedia is the primary source.

Hard call: a parliamentary system would point to the prime minister, but on 1 Jan 1990 the executive was directed by Civic Forum through Havel (elected unanimously by the Federal Assembly 29 Dec 1989), while PM Calfa was still nominally KSC (he left the party for VPN on 18 Jan 1990). Choosing Calfa would make the ruling bloc Communist at the start, which the Government of National Understanding was not. Calfa's party field is his formal membership on 1 Jan 1990.
Parliamentary monarchy: the prime minister directs the executive.
Third presidency began 16 Aug 1986; he stood again in May 1990, so no hard term bound him and must_leave_by is null.
Single four-year term, no immediate re-election.
The president governs; the prime minister is his appointee. Tie is the NDP (the polity's Party pillar is the same institution), so the seeded ruling bloc is NonAligned per the state-big-tent rule.

Took power in the 3 Aug 1979 coup as chairman of the Supreme Military Council; founded the PDGE in 1987 as the sole legal party, so the party is the tie rather than the Army pillar (which in this polity is the Moroccan guard, not his own institution).

since is the WPE general secretaryship (12 Sep 1984), the office that carried power; the PDRE presidency followed on 10 Sep 1987. Lieutenant colonel, but by 1990 ruled through the party, so the tie is et_wpe.

Recalled 5 Dec 1987 to head the post-coup interim administration; Alliance Party leader, so tied to the dormant fj_alliance row rather than to the Army pillar Rabuka commanded. Ganilau's presidential start is 8 Dec 1987 on Wikipedia and 5 Dec 1987 on worldstatesmen; Wikipedia's date is used. Rabuka (RFMF commander, 1987-Apr 1991) omitted from also because no source fetched gave a day-precise start.

Decided case in the design: Mitterrand with Rocard in also. Re-election was permitted in 1990 so no must_leave_by.

Presidential start is 2 Dec 1967 on Wikipedia, 28 Nov 1967 on worldstatesmen; Wikipedia used. Head of the PDG single-party regime, so tied to ga_pdg rather than the Party pillar (the PDG Bureau Politique) - same bloc either way.

The Germany roster entry is the Federal Republic; the GDR still existed on 1 Jan 1990 and its head of government (Modrow, SED) is recorded in also as a fact of that date. His party is not in the polity table so party is null.

Hardest call. The polity's ruling prose is 'the rival cabinets of Michel Aoun and Selim Hoss'. Hrawi, elected 24 Nov 1989 by 47 of 53 deputies at Chtoura in the Syrian-held Bekaa, is the head of state whom the Hoss cabinet recognised and the one the outside world recognised; the Taif accord had not yet moved executive power to the cabinet in practice. The polity has no parties and Hrawi was an independent Maronite, so the tie is to the pillar his government actually rested on: the Syrian Army (Security). Aoun's rival administration lasted until 13 Oct 1990.
